claims.text: itch.io provides game-page hosting, downloads, checkout/distribution and creator-side usage information.
claims.limitations: This describes platform roles, not revenue, reach or sales volume.

claims.text: A newly created project is private by default and can be made public through its visibility settings.
claims.limitations: Publishing is separate from search/browse indexing and buyer acquisition.

claims.text: Creator documentation says project-page creation, hosting and uploads do not require an upfront listing fee.
claims.limitations: No platform listing charge does not mean zero development, payment or tax costs.

claims.text: Sellers can use direct-to-seller payment collection or collected-by-itch.io payouts; the two routes differ in merchant-of-record status and tax/chargeback handling.
claims.limitations: Jurisdiction and processor configuration can affect a specific account.

claims.text: The platform-share slider supports 0–100% with a documented default illustration of 10%.
claims.limitations: The 10% share is a default/example, not a fixed compulsory rate and not a measured seller average.

claims.text: Official USD example models a $10 buyer payment less $1 platform share and $0.59 processor cost, producing $8.41 before other deductions.
claims.limitations: Illustrative 2.9% + $0.30 fees are not a guaranteed processor schedule and are not net profit.

claims.text: itch.io describes its dashboard gross revenue as total amount buyers paid before deductions.
claims.limitations: Dashboard gross is neither available payout nor seller profit.

claims.text: The platform documents PayPal and Stripe for payment processing and does not itself store buyer payment card information.
claims.limitations: Available methods, fees and account eligibility may vary by locale and route.

claims.text: Direct-payment sellers connect payment providers and are merchant of record; their provider receives individual transactions.
claims.limitations: Availability depends on seller provider onboarding and payment-country rules.

claims.text: With collected payments itch.io is merchant of record, handles payout requests and documented EU VAT collection/remittance.
claims.limitations: Does not resolve individual seller income taxes, non-EU taxes, or other legal obligations.

claims.text: Collected payouts require an eligible balance of at least $5, tax interview, configured payout method and a seven-day transaction hold.
claims.limitations: These are conditions, not a guaranteed payment date; adjustments and review can delay funds.

claims.text: Staff review collected payout requests, requiring at least seven days after request and commonly 10–14 days; first-time or flagged sellers may wait longer.
claims.limitations: Does not establish a universally applicable first-payment completion date.

claims.text: Collected sellers are limited to three outstanding payout requests, with further fees possible on transfer and long-unclaimed balances.
claims.limitations: Exact final payout fees and individual jurisdiction outcomes are unspecified.

claims.text: Collected payment mode is denominated in USD; direct mode permits configured currencies conditional on processor settings.
claims.limitations: This is not a claim that any particular non-US account is approved or receives local-currency settlement.

claims.text: Paid project minimums permit higher voluntary buyer payments; free/donation projects may be downloaded without paying.
claims.limitations: The 2015 historical aggregate extra-payment statistic on the documentation page is not used as a current platform estimate.

claims.text: The pricing documentation distinguishes free downloads without payment from ownership entitlements granted after payment.
claims.limitations: Ownership is a platform file-access concept; it does not prove legal IP ownership.

claims.text: Individually priced files can require additional paid thresholds, and their entitlement differs from basic project-level ownership.
claims.limitations: Individual file minimum changes may affect continued buyer access to that file.

claims.text: The storefront supports timed sales, bundles and paid-file levels, with cooperative multi-seller bundles conditioned on payment mode.
claims.limitations: Support for a sales mechanism is not evidence that any promotion increases profit.

claims.text: To qualify for indexing, a public project normally needs a cover image plus an available paid, downloadable or browser-playable product.
claims.limitations: Meeting baseline rules does not guarantee ranking, discoverability or purchases.

claims.text: First-time paid sellers can have a published page available by direct URL while search/browse indexing awaits review.
claims.limitations: The guide generally describes review in business days; it is not an SLA for any given seller.

claims.text: itch.io states that direct title search and topical tag-based browsing are distinct discovery mechanisms.
claims.limitations: No public formula, impressions or paid conversion observations established.

claims.text: itch.io specifically cautions that recent-release listings alone are ineffective as a game discovery strategy.
claims.limitations: Editorial guidance, not a measured causal estimate or market-wide acquisition cost.

claims.text: Official guidance describes project followers, devlogs, updates and email notifications as promotion/retention mechanisms.
claims.limitations: Mechanism availability is not measured retained buyer count or incremental sales.

claims.text: The seller dashboard provides overview and deeper counts for page views, downloads and purchases.
claims.limitations: Owner-only metrics cannot be treated as public seller distributions.

claims.text: HTML5 games can run inside an embedded frame from a single HTML file or zip containing an index.html entry point.
claims.limitations: Technical ability does not imply any browser player purchases the game.

claims.text: Jam submissions are itch.io project pages with distinct jam submission records and optional ratings; they are not paid transactions.
claims.limitations: No representative jam-to-paid purchase conversion follows from these mechanics.

claims.text: The creator FAQ says publishers retain ownership of content and itch.io receives only the rights needed to host and show it.
claims.limitations: Third-party game assets, work-for-hire terms and IP disputes require independent review.

claims.text: The creator FAQ describes distribution of uploaded files without adding itch.io DRM.
claims.limitations: A seller's own DRM or external access requirements are not ruled out by this statement.

claims.text: Buyer emails are available through project interaction controls after a first sale with an at-most-daily send limit.
claims.limitations: Does not document repeat-purchase rates or transferable mailing-list rights.

claims.text: The platform can deindex low-quality or policy-violating projects without necessarily making their direct URLs unreachable.
claims.limitations: Documentation is not an estimate of the frequency of deindexing or commercial losses.

claims.text: On October 26, 2026, the default itch.io Games browse showed 1,780,861 results.
claims.limitations: Dynamic browse results include free and paid game listings; not an active seller or buyer count.

claims.text: On October 26, 2026, the itch.io paid Games filter showed 49,588 results.
claims.limitations: Paid-listing availability does not prove a game has made any paid sales.

claims.text: On October 26, 2026, itch.io Games tagged 2D showed 428,856 results.
claims.limitations: Tag-based classification overlaps with other genres; not a verified commercial 2D audience.

claims.text: In a December 2025 voluntary devlog, one developer reported 17,000 itch.io page views, 414 sales, and USD 706.73 in total itch.io revenue for a game.
claims.limitations: Self-reported single-title figures; sample selected by publisher, revenue accounting and observation window not independently audited.

claims.text: A December 2025 developer retrospective reported lifetime 52,217 game page views, 4,763 game downloads, 19,548 game browser plays and USD 24 game-category revenue.
claims.limitations: Game-category subset of a multiproduct publishing account; voluntary self-report, not individual product or population income data.

claims.text: A developer reported two distinct pay-what-you-want page payments of USD 25 and USD 2 before fees, alongside roughly USD 760 in separate cooperative bundle proceeds for the game.
claims.limitations: A narrative 2020–2021 case with heterogeneous transaction routes, no profit audit, and no inference to current typical paid-game outcomes.

claims.text: In July 2025, itch.io publicly attributed a broad adult-content discovery deindexing action to scrutiny from payment processors.
claims.limitations: Historical event for adult-content browse/search; no claim about all genres or lost sales.

claims.text: On July 31, 2025, itch.io announced reindexing free adult NSFW pages configured with No Payments, while indicating paid categories would return cautiously.
claims.limitations: Historical update, not independently verified current availability or payout eligibility in October 2026.

claims.text: Current published creator rules warn that certain misclassified or prohibited content can cause search deindexing, suspension or disabled merchant payments.
claims.limitations: Actual enforcement frequency, seller loss and account-specific appeal rights remain unmeasured.

claims.text: itch.io's quality guidance warns that stripping buyers of paid-content access without continued access can lead to suspension, refunds and payout cancellation.
claims.limitations: Conditional policy enforcement, not a documented rate of refund or seller closure.

claims.text: Single-seller promotions may include discounts and multiple items sold for one optional bundle price.
claims.limitations: Offer availability does not prove higher demand or profit.

claims.text: An itch.io promotion can use coupon-code access or require an existing item ownership entitlement.
claims.limitations: Does not establish returning-buyer counts or retention effects.

claims.text: A promotion owner can access purchase and earnings analytics for that sale.
claims.limitations: Seller-private analytics cannot stand in for representative public sales.

claims.text: Cooperative game bundles allocate eligible proceeds to participants using relative weights, not full order revenue to every game.
claims.limitations: Must not double-count one aggregate bundle checkout as several standalone sales.

claims.text: Cooperative bundles require participant approval before publishing the specified terms and revenue distribution.
claims.limitations: Documented workflow, not evidence that any particular bundle sold units.

claims.text: Receiving cooperative bundle proceeds requires itch.io payout eligibility even for a seller otherwise set up for direct payments.
claims.limitations: Eligibility is account- and country-dependent; no individual approval inferred.

claims.text: With more than 15 bundled projects, download keys are generated on individual claims, while bundle purchase grants ownership of all included projects.
claims.limitations: Distinct counts: bundle purchases, game entitlements and claimed download keys.

claims.text: Game jams can have ranked voting and ratings, which the operator cautions can favor popular creators or manipulation.
claims.limitations: Jam engagement is not a sale or observed conversion.

claims.text: The HTML5 embedded-game listing type can accept donations but does not natively require payment to play; a downloadable listing is a distinct way to sell access.
claims.limitations: Does not show which model earns more money or whether a user will donate.

claims.text: A browser-playable ZIP needs an index.html entry point at its root and relative paths for supporting assets; a self-contained HTML file is an alternative upload.
claims.limitations: Static packaging instructions, not verification that a given game runs correctly.

claims.text: Published HTML5 ZIP limits include at most 1,000 extracted files, at most 500MB extracted, at most 200MB per file and at most 240 characters in a file path.
claims.limitations: Documented default upload limits can change or be adjusted on request.

claims.text: Browser games can embed in-page or launch fullscreen; mobile pages use fullscreen launch, and Mobile Friendly should be enabled only after real mobile testing.
claims.limitations: Not evidence of mobile platform reach, performance or buyer behavior.

claims.text: The first-page guide recommends a 315:250 cover ratio and three to five screenshots for storefront presentation.
claims.limitations: Editorial guidance, not a causal estimate of clickthrough or conversion.

claims.text: A downloadable game listing may include a separately marked free demo alongside a paid full build and optional higher-tier files.
claims.limitations: Demo downloads are not paid units and do not establish a free-to-paid conversion rate.

claims.text: Game pages have Draft, Restricted and Public visibility modes, distinct from download-key access to individual files.
claims.limitations: A public URL can be unindexed, and visibility does not determine paid entitlement.

claims.text: A future release date can prohibit purchases and downloads until the release date, while a public page can separately disable new downloads or purchases.
claims.limitations: These are configured restrictions, not verified market performance or launch-day sale volumes.

claims.text: Free downloads do not create ownership keys, while paid purchases or manually generated keys can grant persistent product-file access.
claims.limitations: File access is not game IP ownership, a distinct paid unit, or an identified human purchaser.

claims.text: The platform permits external keys as a supplement but discourages pages composed principally of off-site redemption links, potentially affecting indexing.
claims.limitations: A key distributed with a sale does not prove an external-store purchase.

claims.text: Owner-uploaded file changes generally appear on buyer download pages, while individually priced file thresholds may restrict access.
claims.limitations: Does not establish how often customers update or whether updates induce new purchases.

claims.text: The operator allows buyer emails after at least one sale and at most once daily, with unsubscribe mechanisms.
claims.limitations: Communication capability is not evidence of repeated orders, open rates or personal email portability.

claims.text: On 2026-10-26, the itch.io paid games catalog under the 2D tag returned 12,691 browse results.
claims.limitations: Count of live filtered listings; not a verified distinct-developer population or game-sales census.

claims.text: The visible Popular paid-2D listing included discounted titles temporarily displayed at $0 during a 100% promotion.
claims.limitations: A display-listing observation; does not imply these projects have zero lifetime earnings or that a buyer paid zero across all available tiers.

claims.text: A 2025 Gamedev.js community survey received 445 submissions, and 67.4% of the 439 publishing-question respondents selected itch.io or similar sites.
claims.limitations: Self-selected web game developer respondents; combined platform category, not an itch.io market-share or exclusive creator estimate.

claims.text: The 2025 Gamedev.js report describes 63% of responding web-game developers as earning no money from game development, and 15.4% under USD 1,000 annually.
claims.limitations: Based on 435 voluntary respondents to annual game-development income from any source, not a census or representative sample of paid itch.io publishers.

claims.text: The 2024 Gamedev.js report describes 58.2% of its web-game-development respondents as earning no game-development income, with 17.7% under USD 1,000 annually.
claims.limitations: Self-selected 2024 web developer survey; not a representative census of game sellers or itch.io platform earnings.

claims.text: The reported zero-income shares of the 2024 and 2025 Gamedev.js survey samples differ by 4.8 percentage points.
claims.limitations: Difference between two differently sampled voluntary surveys, not verified increase in population-wide zero earners or itch.io sales failure.

claims.text: For collected payments itch.io lists USD checkout and payout settlement, while direct collection uses a seller-selected provider-compatible currency.
claims.limitations: Account-specific processor fees, conversion and final recipient currency still vary.

claims.text: Stripe lists Mexico as a generally supported Stripe operating country, but itch.io's own direct Stripe country/currency examples omit Mexico.
claims.limitations: Cannot infer that itch.io direct Stripe integration works for a specific Mexico-based seller; generic Stripe support is not an itch.io integration guarantee.

claims.text: PayPal Mexico says funds received can be automatically transferred to a linked CLABE bank account with MXN conversion when applicable and foreign-exchange fees.
claims.limitations: Individual payout eligibility, currency settlement, bank compatibility and actual exchange rates are not known.

claims.text: Stripe Mexico's official support page says domestic charges from Mexican cards must be in MXN.
claims.limitations: Processor country rule does not determine itch.io's own seller currency settings or a given seller's account status.

claims.text: itch.io requires collected sellers to complete an identity/tax interview, validate information before payment, and describes a default 30% withholding when adequate tax identification is absent.
claims.limitations: This is platform documentation, not tax advice or proof of a final withholding rate for any individual seller, jurisdiction, income classification or treaty claim.

claims.text: itch.io publicly documents PayPal/Payoneer collected payouts and separate direct processor accounts; the official documentation alone does not establish whether any particular Mexican seller can complete an approved payout.
claims.limitations: External provider support is not an eligibility confirmation and no real seller account onboarding was attempted.

claims.text: itch.io's seller guide identifies product pages, embedded purchase widgets and a JavaScript buy popup as separate ways to initiate the same purchase flow.
claims.limitations: Documented entry paths, not observed traffic shares or completed sales.

claims.text: The purchase dialog allows buyer payments above an item minimum and supports individually priced files, optional tips and gift purchases.
claims.limitations: A displayed price is not the settled amount in each transaction; selected bonuses and promotions differ.

claims.text: Successful payment creates a download-key URL with file access, email receipt and an optional later connection to a buyer account.
claims.limitations: Download key creation is not evidence of a separate game purchase in bundle claims or owner-issued keys.

claims.text: An itch.io account is not required for a buyer to purchase a game, and purchases are associated with an email address.
claims.limitations: Logged-in accounts are not a census of unique buyers; no personally identifying purchaser data was collected.

claims.text: Buyers can revisit a key URL to redownload updated files and can claim optional external keys; these actions are distinct from new paid orders.
claims.limitations: Repeat file access is not a repeat purchase or evidence of retention revenue.

claims.text: The server-side itch.io API requires an account API key and OAuth requests need user authorization for delegated access.
claims.limitations: Not evidence that aggregate developer sales are available without account consent, and no token was accessed.

claims.text: itch.io documents public RSS feeds for browse results, new releases, featured releases and sales, but these feeds do not provide merchant transaction histories.
claims.limitations: Public project feeds measure releases/visibility and cannot establish seller median profit or purchaser cohorts.

claims.text: A 2025 How To Market A Game survey reports 169 itch.io developers voluntarily submitted project traffic statistics.
claims.limitations: Nonrandom submissions; number of distinct games in every chart and percentage of commercial paid games unknown.

claims.text: The author reports median 1,582 lifetime page views among participating itch.io games and a heavily skewed mean near 54,483.
claims.limitations: Nonrepresentative project cohort with varying game ages; view events are not unique visitors or buyers.

claims.text: The same article prints median 590 browser plays and 110 downloads in a mixed-format comparison table.
claims.limitations: May be format-mixed, differing sample denominators; events not buyers. Does not establish causal browser uplift.

claims.text: The article's download mean is 6,017 in its Download section and 58,976 in its combined All stats table; its view percentiles also differ by section.
claims.limitations: The published discrepancy is preserved without assuming which figure is a transcription or sample error.

claims.text: The 2025 itch.io traffic benchmark reports views, browser plays and downloads, not a representative distribution of settled game revenue or developer profit.
claims.limitations: Interpretive claims about universal lack of itch.io earnings cannot be established from these traffic figures.

claims.text: One developer's annual published retrospectives report lifetime game-category views, downloads, browser plays and game revenue for 2023, 2024 and 2025.
claims.limitations: Repeated observations of one voluntarily reporting account, not three statistically independent creators or all paid games.

claims.text: The account reported 21,174 cumulative game page views, 3,992 game downloads, 5,871 browser plays and USD 0 lifetime game-category revenue by the end of 2024.
claims.limitations: Free/donation-led game portfolio, no audited costs or net profit and no individual buyer information.

claims.text: By December 2025 the same account reported 52,217 cumulative game page views, 4,763 game downloads, 19,548 browser plays and USD 24 game revenue.
claims.limitations: Increased attention and low paid receipts are co-observed, not evidence of causal conversion failure or an average platform outcome.

claims.text: The account's games generated no reported game-category revenue in its 2023 and 2024 lifetime snapshots while other categories such as fonts generated its main commercial receipts.
claims.limitations: Product-mix, tip-based pricing and individual accounting are specific to this creator; does not establish typical mandatory paid-game demand.

claims.text: A 2021 developer postmortem reports 1,776 itch.io paid units and $17,906 gross for Mixolumia.
claims.limitations: Historic voluntary case; not audited typical earnings or profit.

claims.text: The same developer reports 713 Steam units and $6,202 gross, and later after-transaction receipts of $14,980 from itch.io and $3,680 from Steam.
claims.limitations: Unequal store launch windows and settlement lag; receipts exclude labor and development costs.

claims.text: The Mixolumia developer explicitly noted continuing contract work and development effort beyond transaction deductions.
claims.limitations: No measured hourly game-development wage or audited profit.

claims.text: Foxglove Games described approximately €85,000 associated with Trouble Comes Twice across Kickstarter, Patreon, pre-sales and game sales.
claims.limitations: Multi-channel amount, not itch.io-only earnings, and not the founders' personal net income.

claims.text: itch.io's butler tool pushes a folder or ZIP to a named release channel and uses difference-based patch uploads when updating an existing channel.
claims.limitations: Descriptive platform functionality, no specific game bandwidth savings proved.

claims.text: On the first butler push all required assets must be transferred, while later changes can use incremental patches and optimized background processing.
claims.limitations: Percentage savings examples vary by actual changed files and compression.

claims.text: The butler pushing guide states that the backend rejects builds above 30 GB uncompressed.
claims.limitations: Documented limit not tested against any new game; future revisions possible.

claims.text: Butler supports named channels such as Linux and Windows releases and optional publisher version labels, with channel updates visible before fully optimized patches finish.
claims.limitations: No account authorization or actual upload was attempted.

claims.text: itch.io's Linux publishing guide recommends portable archives, bundling needed runtime dependencies without bundling graphics drivers or glibc, and testing GLIBC compatibility.
claims.limitations: Engine exports vary and documentation does not validate any specific executable.

claims.text: The itch Linux guide describes compiling against older GLIBC or fully static musl as compatibility approaches, subject to game/library suitability.
claims.limitations: Approach is not proof a particular Rust or C++ game runs on every target distro.

claims.text: An itch.io May 2026 announcement added a graphical butler build-upload workflow inside the itch app, with change preview and channels.
claims.limitations: The feature requires app versions/settings and seller authentication; this research did not open the app.

claims.text: Multi-platform packaging and QA, incremental uploads, version management and player update support are real release processes separate from the storefront's price-share fees.
claims.limitations: No average person-hours, bug cost or typical publisher expense is quantified.

claims.text: The published terms distinguish users age over 13 from publishers over 18 or with legally sufficient parental/guardian consent and capacity.
claims.limitations: General 2023-last-updated published terms; not a verified determination of any individual legal capacity.

claims.text: Publishers retain rights in their uploaded games, while granting itch.io a worldwide non-exclusive royalty-free sublicenseable/transferable license to host, redistribute and promote the content in connection with the service.
claims.limitations: Does not determine rights in third-party images, engines, music or contractors; the service's licensed uses are wider than merely displaying a store cover.

claims.text: The published itch.io content-license grant is non-exclusive, so it does not itself impose a blanket prohibition on also distributing content elsewhere.
claims.limitations: Independent product, publisher, publisher-licensing and third-party rights obligations may still restrict specific titles.

claims.text: Itch.io requires publishers to warrant adequate ownership, permissions, licenses and consent for uploaded/distributed games and incorporated media.
claims.limitations: No verification of actual third-party assets, art, fonts, engine licenses, marks or music was performed.

claims.text: The published legal terms provide a DMCA notice and counter-notification workflow; responding can entail identifying the publisher to a claimant.
claims.limitations: Not legal advice, no private case handled, dispute duration and result are not guaranteed.

claims.text: Published terms permit refunds for unavailable/unplayable/misdescribed content and explain that external-key products can require confirming key cancellation.
claims.limitations: Buyer eligibility and transaction reversals differ by circumstance, seller mode, and law; no observed refund rate.

claims.text: Collected publisher account earnings from transactions older than 12 months and not claimed for withdrawal can be subject to a maintenance debit of 10% of original revenue per aging purchase per month.
claims.limitations: Conditional unclaimed-earnings provision, not a standard transaction fee or tax applied to every seller; publisher can contact support.

claims.text: The stated unclaimed-earnings charge stops at zero and does not create negative merchant balances.
claims.limitations: A 2023-last-updated published contract clause, not proof of account-specific application or historical debits.

claims.text: The creator FAQ prohibits public or third-party sharing of identifiable buyer dashboard details including email, name, IP, country code and transaction identifiers.
claims.limitations: Seller records and low-count quasi-identifying aggregates must not be exposed; no buyer data accessed.

claims.text: itch.io requires explicit buyer opt-in before mailing-list enrollment and reserves provided buyer email contact for transaction-related messages.
claims.limitations: Not verification of a specific email campaign or buyer consent basis.

claims.text: The creator FAQ warns that certain payment-processor/content policy violations may freeze or refund transactions and make funds ineligible for payout.
claims.limitations: Risk route, not evidence of current seller suspensions or losses.

claims.text: Quality violations can remove a project from searchable browse discovery without necessarily disabling its direct-link page.
claims.limitations: No frequency of deindexing or causal effect on paid game outcomes observed.

claims.text: itch.io supports optional time-based one-time password (TOTP) second-factor authentication configured through the account's security settings.
claims.limitations: An available feature, not observed adoption, security success probability or enabled status.

claims.text: The site documents generated account recovery codes for loss of the authentication device and says SMS-based two-factor login is not offered.
claims.limitations: No recovery code was generated or viewed; do not store publisher security tokens or keys.

claims.text: The official indexing guide says newly published first-time paid sellers may be held for moderator review before their public game appears in Search and Browse.
claims.limitations: Published direct-link functionality and seller earnings ability are distinct from guaranteed search index placement.

claims.text: The official discovery guide states the original game publication date is not reset by updates or later indexing and discourages recreating pages to bypass restrictions.
claims.limitations: Not a measured effect on unit sales or causal launch timing uplift.

claims.text: The guide distinguishes direct-title text search, optimized for known-name lookup, from tag-driven browse discovery for topics and genres.
claims.limitations: The document describes product policy but provides no public query volumes or paid conversion rates.

claims.text: itch.io distinguishes generative-AI-assisted creation from traditional procedural algorithms, NPC logic and dynamic difficulty; AI-generated materials should use the project AI Disclosure setting.
claims.limitations: Terms and enforcement may evolve; no game, tool or training-data compliance audit was performed.

claims.text: The quality guidance states that generative-AI disclosure is strictly enforced for game asset pages, with delisting possible for failures.
claims.limitations: This asset-category enforcement does not establish a platform-wide ban on all AI-assisted games.

claims.text: The guidelines warn against mass-generated near-identical game pages or works dominated by minimally curated generated content.
claims.limitations: No measured prevalence of delisted AI games or revenue effects.

claims.text: Platform tags should represent directly running, actually tested builds, not merely emulator support or the operating system capable of opening an archive.
claims.limitations: A tag is not a compatibility certification; no binaries were tested.

claims.text: Games should select only languages they actually contain; no-text projects should use the appropriate accessibility classification rather than claiming all languages.
claims.limitations: This is a metadata requirement, not evidence localization increases purchases.

claims.text: The guide prefers appropriate recommended tags and avoiding duplicate synonyms and self-promotional irrelevant classifications.
claims.limitations: No tagged-query traffic volumes, ranking formula or causal conversion data available.

claims.text: Entering unrelated game jams, creating a game jam solely to promote a product, or using jams to seize participants' IP are discouraged and may lead to platform restrictions.
claims.limitations: This does not determine commercial returns from genuine jam participation.

claims.text: Publisher guidance discourages permanent/fake markdowns, inflated base prices followed by discounts and very frequent sales; evergreen multi-game bundle discounts are distinguished.
claims.limitations: No observed demand elasticity, annual seller sale frequency or discount lift established.

claims.text: Followers can receive notices about new publisher projects, devlogs and sales of projects they do not already own.
claims.limitations: Follower count is not an active buyer count; delivery/open rates, purchase conversion and incremental sales unmeasured.

claims.text: Publisher-side Interact tools show ratings and press links, while comments and discussion boards offer user participation and moderation.
claims.limitations: Public review/press presence is not a proxy for paid orders or profit.

claims.text: Limited playtests can use restricted access, password or invite-only settings and limited download keys without placing an unfinished release in public storefront discovery.
claims.limitations: Tool availability is not evidence that playtests improve long-run sales.

claims.text: The limited-release guide describes wharf/butler binary patching for pre-release testers and automatic updates in the itch app.
claims.limitations: No game was uploaded; bandwidth, testing labor and retention effects not quantified.

claims.text: itch.io's limited-release guide warns that publicly launching unfinished early-access projects may create reputation risk and spend the initial release's attention peak.
claims.limitations: Qualitative guidance, not a measured causal early-access sales penalty.

claims.text: The quality guide recommends representative screenshots and covers and avoiding seizure-triggering animations or deceptive images.
claims.limitations: Not measured effect on revenue, accessibility or page conversion.

claims.text: The 2013 creator-facing announcement offered customizable indie game listings, file hosting and optional minimum prices.
claims.limitations: Early feature state, not observed publisher population.

claims.text: In January 2015 itch.io launched collected seller payouts partly to simplify EU VAT for eligible sellers.
claims.limitations: Historical policy, not present-day tax compliance advice.

claims.text: In March 2015 itch.io announced configurable 0–100% platform share with a 10% default, planned to activate on March 23.
claims.limitations: Not observed seller-choice distribution.

claims.text: In February 2018 itch.io introduced impressions and click-through measurements in owner analytics.
claims.limitations: Historical product launch, not a public game sales dataset.

claims.text: At introduction, impression and CTR summaries covered only the preceding week while other project analytics supported longer periods.
claims.limitations: Historical initial limitation; current 2026 window has not been independently reverified.

claims.text: The original analytics announcement defined an impression as a project thumbnail/title shown in browsing or recommended surfaces, with CTR indicating subsequent page clicks.
claims.limitations: Neither metric identifies unique people or paid buyers.

claims.text: In July 2026 itch.io launched seasonal Sale Explorer filtering including tag exclusion, final price, staff picks and recommendations.
claims.limitations: Not a guarantee these features apply to all ordinary browsing year-round.

claims.text: During the July 2026 Summer Sale the operator reported more than 30,000 discounted projects across marketplace categories.
claims.limitations: Mixed game and non-game project listings; not purchases, sales or paid customers.

claims.text: A July 2026 update refreshed cooperative bundle drafting and introduced ratio-based share allocation with two decimal places.
claims.limitations: Technical mechanism, not evidence of bundle revenue volume.

claims.text: The July 2026 Patreon integration introduced membership-tier access grants and gifted-tier support.
claims.limitations: Patreon receipts are external membership money, not native itch.io game orders.

claims.text: In 2019 one game artist reported 34 itch.io interactive works, all available freely with optional payment.
claims.limitations: This is not a positive-price paid-game seller sample.

claims.text: The artist reported $7,276.70 accumulated gross revenue with $7,164.18 attributed to tips.
claims.limitations: Optional gifts are not mandatory premium unit sales or labor-adjusted profit.

claims.text: The 2019 writeup alternately reports 1,072 and 1,073 cumulative payments.
claims.limitations: Preserve source inconsistency; neither count is a verified audit.

claims.text: The artist credited press coverage and repeated smaller releases with some traffic and donations.
claims.limitations: Self-described correlation is not proof of causal acquired buyers.

claims.text: The retrieved itch.io Paid Puzzle genre page showed 7,456 paid-filter listing results.
claims.limitations: Recently indexed non-synchronized listing count, not observed game sales, unique creators or paid buyers.

claims.text: The retrieved itch.io Paid Horror tag page showed 5,117 paid-filter listing results.
claims.limitations: Recently indexed non-synchronized listing count, not observed game sales, unique creators or paid buyers.

claims.text: The retrieved itch.io Paid Cozy tag page showed 857 paid-filter listing results.
claims.limitations: Recently indexed non-synchronized listing count, not observed game sales, unique creators or paid buyers.

claims.text: itch.io jam guidance permits a project to have multiple collaborators and describes separately configurable jam host, judge and moderator privileges.
claims.limitations: Contributors and a single seller account cannot be assumed to be independent earning developers.

claims.text: In a 2018 support response the itch.io administrator described allowing page admins to display a shared game on their profiles and manually creating an account for teams.
claims.limitations: Historical operator guidance; current project administration and earnings privileges are not reverified from a live account.

claims.text: Cooperative bundle revenue shares are allocated to participating owner accounts, not automatically to every individual collaborator on a single game's project.
claims.limitations: Cannot infer legal contributor compensation or joint IP ownership from public page administration.

claims.text: itch.io describes publishing and hosting projects without a compulsory upfront listing fee, while separate payment processing applies to transactions.
claims.limitations: No cash listing fee does not imply no asset, testing, tax, refund, labor or game development costs.

claims.text: itch.io broadly accepts games online, but seller payment eligibility, settlement currencies and buyers' access should be studied in independent geographic frames.
claims.limitations: A worldwide accessible page is not proof of worldwide compatible payout and legal eligibility.

claims.text: itch.io supports playable browser projects and downloadable paid games as distinct release types; a minimal 2D demo's scope alone cannot establish buyer demand.
claims.limitations: Game length, mechanics and production budget used in scenarios are hypothetical and have no sales measurements.

claims.text: An October 2026 game software-engineering paper analyzed 491 selected itch.io games matched to accessible public GitHub source repositories after screening a prior 10,548-project dataset.
claims.limitations: Sample selection excludes most commercial, closed-source and unmatched projects; not a random paid publisher census.

claims.text: The curated 491-game source sample had 103 Puzzle, 97 Action and 69 Platformer labels, with genres potentially overlapping.
claims.limitations: Counts apply only to the open-source sample, not market-wide genre supply or commercial demand.

claims.text: 289 of the paper's 491 GitHub-matched itch.io games had no player ratings (58.9% of its corpus).
claims.limitations: No rating is not evidence of zero downloads, zero purchasers, or zero creator income.

claims.text: Repository signature detection identified Godot in 120 and Unity in 84 of 491 sampled open-source games; engines were undetected in 231.
claims.limitations: Source-code signature estimates and incomplete tags cannot become all-itch.io game engine market shares.

claims.text: The authors manually verified automated test suites in 36 of 491 open-source itch.io game repositories after 111 candidates were initially flagged.
claims.limitations: 7.33% sample rate not platform-wide testing prevalence and not an indicator of commercial success.

claims.text: In the curated open-source corpus, test files were associated with higher repository commit activity, but were not significantly associated with game ratings after statistical controls.
claims.limitations: Observational adjusted association is not a causal benefit for player ratings, production time, sales or developer profit.

claims.text: The 491 selected game repositories averaged 74.35 GitHub stars and 4.22 contributors, with large right-skew.
claims.limitations: GitHub stars, contributors and repository commits are not paid customers, game units sold, salaries or hours worked.

claims.text: The 2026 engineering paper's development variables cannot answer the share of paid games making money or estimate the median income from selling games on itch.io.
claims.limitations: The source does not contain representative positive-price checkout transactions or costs.

claims.text: On September 26, 2026 a community analyst described voluntarily collected analytics of 690 itch.io games, expanding the author's earlier 145-game sample.
claims.limitations: Nonrandom overlapping snapshots; no representative eligible paid publisher frame.

claims.text: The later 690-record sample was reported to have median 750 lifetime page views, 88 downloads, and a $0 revenue label.
claims.limitations: Median is a published descriptor of voluntary mixed game observations, not representative median of positive-price games.

claims.text: The author reported 45% of contributed game records earning no revenue, while also reporting a median $0 amount.
claims.limitations: Arithmetic or measurement ambiguity with median requires rounding/definition clarification; not population-wide zero sales.

claims.text: For the 690 voluntarily disclosed game records, the author reported about one in seven above $100 reported game revenue and seven entries above $1,000.
claims.limitations: Self-reported, unverified figures may include gifts and bundle allocations, not profit; later comments updated counts.

claims.text: The author estimated the top tenth of the 690 submitted games received around 93% of sample page views.
claims.limitations: Creator-reported sample concentration, not whole-market buyer, purchase or payout concentration.

claims.text: In the self-selected 690-record sample, the author reported 47 browser plays per 100 view events versus 16 downloads per 100 view events.
claims.limitations: Different offer types and submission cohorts, not causal paid game conversion or unique people.

claims.text: The analyst's September 16 initial 145-game median figures and September 26 690-game figures describe growing overlapping snapshots, not two independent developer samples.
claims.limitations: Cannot compare their percentiles as a time trend, changed composition changes summary.

claims.text: The benchmark collector openly acknowledged self-selection and that publisher-shared game stats may overrepresent games with unusually high traffic.
claims.limitations: It does not follow that a randomly sampled paid game would perform at or below the reported median.

claims.text: Semrush modeled approximately 162.37 million visits to the entire itch.io domain during September 2026, compared with 174.43 million in August and 161.31 million in July.
claims.limitations: This is third-party modeled visits to all marketplace categories, not unique people, game purchases or confirmed first-party traffic.

claims.text: For September 2026 Semrush attributed an estimated 26.9% of domain visits to the United States, 6.32% to Brazil, and 4.21% to Bangladesh.
claims.limitations: Modeled session geography, not proportions of paid buyers, paying sellers, game developers or income.

claims.text: Semrush estimated 47.09% direct and 31.97% from google.com among desktop referral pathways for itch.io.
claims.limitations: This is a modeled desktop source estimate, not all-device acquisition shares or observed checkout conversion.

claims.text: The independent whole-site traffic estimate does not establish itch.io's paid-game purchasing population or how many game publishers earn money.
claims.limitations: Analytical boundary drawn from vendor data scope and official mixed-product platform descriptions.

claims.text: The Gamedev.js Survey 2025 was fielded December 8–19, 2025 and released January 27, 2026; its annual game-development income question received 435 answers out of 445 total survey submissions.
claims.limitations: 435 respondents to all-channel income, not itch.io-specific mandatory game transactions.

claims.text: itch.io's collected-payment payout adjustments include a one-time USD $3 tax identity verification fee charged to the publisher account.
claims.limitations: A documented account charge, distinct from a universal upfront listing fee, transaction fee, income-tax liability or repeated per-order deduction.

claims.text: The platform recommends a minimum price around USD $2 to reduce the relative impact of payment providers' fixed per-transaction charges.
claims.limitations: Platform guidance, not a required minimum, price sensitivity experiment, or evidence buyers will pay this price.

claims.text: itch.io's founder reported over USD 100,000 had been paid to developers since the 2013 launch through August 2014.
claims.limitations: Historical cumulative lower bound, not 2026 GMV, annual payout or developer income distribution.

claims.text: The founder reported 13% of registered accounts had uploaded a public game and 7% had linked a payment provider.
claims.limitations: Registered accounts included buyers and jam participants; not an eligible paid-game publisher census.

claims.text: Among public-game publishers with connected payment providers, about 30% had received at least one purchase, including payments for free games.
claims.limitations: Not the probability a 2026 first positive-price game sells, not a median, and not a living-wage rate.

claims.text: Roughly 84% of all purchase events in the founder's 2014 report were generated through off-site referrals rather than itch.io internal browsing.
claims.limitations: Historical purchase-route share, not modern website visits or causal marketing conversion.

claims.text: In the historical 2014 data roughly 11% of purchases occurred while a game was marked on sale.
claims.limitations: Not causal evidence of discount-driven extra purchases or net income.

claims.text: The founder described a $2 historical median list price, median $2 extra among voluntary overpayers of paid games, and median $3 amount paid by paying supporters of free-minimum games.
claims.limitations: Separate conditional groups, not current paid game price or realized typical revenue.

claims.text: The founder reported about 73% of external purchases used game pages and 27% embedded widgets, with a different denominator from all visits.
claims.limitations: Not user-level conversion, unique buyers or modern web checkout shares.

claims.text: The public itch.io Terms prohibit selling, assigning or transferring a user account, with termination an available consequence.
claims.limitations: An account restriction does not itself establish whether all individual digital game entitlements may legally be resold.

claims.text: The Terms provide purchasers a non-exclusive perpetual content-access license through supported functionality, which survives a publisher's removal of that content.
claims.limitations: This is not transfer of developer copyright nor a guarantee of unsupported technical access or an individual game's license.

claims.text: The documented purchase flow supports gifting a game directly at checkout.
claims.limitations: Checkout gifting does not imply resale of an already purchased and installed game.

claims.text: The unique download key URL should not be shared and free downloads do not generate purchased ownership entitlements.
claims.limitations: Download key possession/issuance differs from individual purchasers and the number of paid orders.

claims.text: A buyer may redownload and receive updated files through the existing purchase page without creating a new paid game order.
claims.limitations: Re-download events cannot proxy commercial sales or market size.

claims.text: The general itch.io site terms and buyer help reviewed here do not establish a blanket secondary-market game license transfer mechanism.
claims.limitations: Actual resale rights may depend on product EULA, relevant legal jurisdiction, and facts not contained in the sources.

claims.text: A first-commercial-game postmortem for Crumbling World reported 7 itch.io sales yielding USD 102.83 in roughly its first month.
claims.limitations: One voluntarily reported 2020 launch; unknown platform-wide zero-sale or profitability distribution.

claims.text: The same first-month developer postmortem reported 132 Steam units yielding USD 1,242, 2 Apple Store units yielding USD 29.99, and zero Game Jolt units, compared with seven itch units.
claims.limitations: Different storefront release timing and marketing exposure; amount labelled yielded without standardized gross/net accounting.

claims.text: Crumbling World's developer reported spending approximately USD 10,000 on a marketing agency during a broader launch and generating USD 1,380.82 total reported cross-store sales receipts in the first month.
claims.limitations: No complete development and tax-cost reconciliation; agency spending applies to the overall campaign and must not be assigned wholly to itch.io.

claims.text: The same developer attributed early refunds and poor reviews to crash bugs following a rushed launch, with nine post-release patches in the first month.
claims.limitations: Developer's retrospective assessment; no audited refund quantity, causal marketing estimate or measured platform reliability probability.

claims.text: Crumbling World won a game-jam prize before the developer chose to expand it into a commercial game; the paid launch still disappointed financially.
claims.limitations: One example that awards or jam praise are not sufficient predictors of market sales.

claims.text: The developer described about three years of learning and building while doing other paid work and recommended smaller first commercial games with more testing.
claims.limitations: No validated development hour ledger or evidence that particular suggested scope causally improves revenue.

claims.text: An independent feed observer recorded 118,017 itch.io games over 152 days through June 2026, describing an average of about 776 first-seen games per day.
claims.limitations: Includes all price models, possible relistings and metadata differences, not verified new first-time positive-price releases.

claims.text: The same observer reported 2,477 of 118,017 tracked games had appeared at least once in the featured feed (approximately 2.1%).
claims.limitations: Featured-feed observations, not a probability of paid sales, commercial seller success or verified random launch cohort.

claims.text: For 6,121 games first seen in one late-January 2026 week, 4,897 (about 80%) had no recorded rating by June.
claims.limitations: No rating is not zero paid units or zero money; the first-seen cohort may include products with differing release and update histories.

claims.text: The feed monitor reported that 57 of 6,121 first-seen late-January games eventually appeared in featured results (under 1% of that cohort).
claims.limitations: Not a paid launch success rate and not a unique buyer measure; featured feed is curated and observational.

claims.text: SuperWEIRD: Idle Automation appeared in the observed featured feed on 112 consecutive days, with 652 sightings from February 20 to June 11, 2026.
claims.limitations: Exceptional selected project with a developed external audience; not an average title or guaranteed reach.

claims.text: The researcher observed that a SuperWEIRD game update was followed by a new appearance in chronological release results, showing why first-sighting and publish timestamps must be distinguished.
claims.limitations: A within-game observation, not proof updates reliably restore every publisher to new release listings.

claims.text: The monitor's game-feed counts, ratings, comments and feature placements measure public attention signals but do not expose eligible merchant purchases or profits.
claims.limitations: Cannot estimate paid-game median seller earnings or fee-adjusted cash flow from visibility statistics.

observations.population: game listings returned by default games browse
observations.limitations: Live catalog filter counts may change or be rounded and are not an audited census. Paid count reflects paid listings, not products with demonstrated sales. 2D tag and price filters overlap; 2D counts cannot be added to all-games totals. Search/browse indexing, private pages, restrictions and non-game products have separate scopes. No representative first-time seller outcomes, per-game income or successful-price distributions are observed.

observations.population: game listings returned by positive-price browse filter
observations.limitations: Live catalog filter counts may change or be rounded and are not an audited census. Paid count reflects paid listings, not products with demonstrated sales. 2D tag and price filters overlap; 2D counts cannot be added to all-games totals. Search/browse indexing, private pages, restrictions and non-game products have separate scopes. No representative first-time seller outcomes, per-game income or successful-price distributions are observed.

observations.population: game listings returned under self-assigned 2D tag
observations.limitations: Live catalog filter counts may change or be rounded and are not an audited census. Paid count reflects paid listings, not products with demonstrated sales. 2D tag and price filters overlap; 2D counts cannot be added to all-games totals. Search/browse indexing, private pages, restrictions and non-game products have separate scopes. No representative first-time seller outcomes, per-game income or successful-price distributions are observed.

observations.population: 2D-tagged game listings returned in Paid-filter browse
observations.limitations: Paid-filter 2D tag intersection is not unique commercial titles sold, publisher count, paid customer count or industry revenue; live dynamic count.

summary: Game-selling research active. Official rules for publication, indexing, payments, pricing, seller analytics, file delivery and game jams are documented. Typical developer sales, zero-earner fraction, median profit and causal discovery effects remain unknown.
